Det övergripande målet med projektet är att bidra till skyddet och bevarandet av minst 25 procent av Albaniens land- och havsområden senast 2030 genom inrättande och förvaltning av ett system för skyddade områden, inklusive Natura 2000-områden och andra områdesbaserade bevarandeåtgärder. Sida-medlen kommer att öronmärkas för specifika aktiviteter inriktade på införlivning av EU-lagstiftning om naturskydd, skydd av särskilt sårbara arter, stödja Natura 2000-processen samt kapacitetsstärkande stöd gällande övervakning, inspektion och verkställighet.
Projektet ska genomföras av UNDP och AICS (Italien) med hjälp av EU-delegerad finansiering om 5,5 MEUR och med ytterligare öronmärkt Sida -finansiering om cirka 2 MEUR. Sida ingår i genomförandekonsortiet som samfinansiär och i projektstyrning, men kommer inte att vara en implementerande part. UNDP är den ledande genomförandepartnern och ansvarig genomförare av Sida-finansierade aktiviteter. Sida har ingått ett bilateralt bidragsavtal med UNDP som reglerar användningen av Sida-medel.

The expected Impact (Overall Objective) of EU for Nature is to contribute to the protection and conservation of at least 25 percent of the Albanian territory (at land and at sea) by 2030 through the establishment and the effective management of a system of Protected Areas (PA), including Natura 2000 sites and other effective area-based conservation measures.
Sida-funding will be earmarked for specific activities targeting the following:
- Full transposition of the Birds and Habitats Directives and supporting the transposition of other EU Acquis in the nature protection as well as development of secondary legislation as part of implementation of legislation.
- Develop and implement action plans for protection of the most vulnerable and important species.
- Advancing the Natura 2000 process by improving knowledge on distribution and status of important habitats and species to facilitate site selection of terrestrial Natura 2000 sites in Albania.
- Strengthen institutional capacities of the relevant authorities in preserving important habitats and species, including performance monitoring, inspection and enforcement.
The EU for Nature project is to be implemented by UNDP and AICS using EU-delegated funding of 5,5 MEUR with additional Sida co-financing in amount of about 2 MEUR. Sida forms part of the implementing consortium and will participate in all project steering and monitoring structures during implementation, but will not be an implementing agency. UNDP is the lead implementing partner and implementer of Sida funding is kept separate from EU funds and regulated through bilateral agreement with UNDP.

description.narrative:
The results analysed here are of the activities that are funded by Sida. There are also activities funded by EU, which are not covered by this assessment.
A.1.1.1 and A.1.1.2: The reference table of species and habitats, prepared in accordance with the annexes of the Birds and Habitats Directives (BHD), along with the accompanying narrative report, has been submitted to the Directorate of Biodiversity at the Ministry of Environment for government adoption. The analysis of remaining legislative gaps has been completed, and drafting of the necessary primary legislation is underway. Work has also commenced on the development of secondary legislation to ensure full alignment with EU requirements.
A.1.1.3: There has been solid progress in strengthening NAPAs revenue generation through the introduction of electronic billing and payment systems. This has improved transparency, reduced informality, and enabled billing for ecosystem services that were previously difficult or impossible to charge for. As a result, NAPAs revenues have increased and are channeled into a ringfenced fund dedicated to financing protection measures. The project has supported the revision of existing regulations governing the use of this fund, including the preparation of a new Decision of the Council of Ministers (DCM). It has also financed the procurement of the equipment required for electronic ticketing which increases efficiency, reduces informality and minimizes the handling of cash. The investment was based on a thorough costbenefit analysis, and maintaining this equipment is clearly in the interest of NAPA and the RAPAs, as the revenues it generates constitute an important element of the resource mobilization strategy for the protected areas network.
A.1.2.3: To date, an inventory of existing draft species action plans (ten in total) has been completed, and gaps have been identified. Two action plans for protected species, the Bear and the Lynx, are currently under development. The reference lists required under the Birds and Habitats Directives (BHD) were added to this component last year and are now completed. They will serve as the basis for identifying Special Areas of Conservation (SACs), Special Protection Areas (SPAs), and for meeting future EU reporting obligations, forming an essential element of Albania's approximation to the Natura 2000 framework. This work was carried out through institutional collaboration between UNDP, the Ministry of Environment, and the Faculty of Natural Sciences.
A.1.3.1: A comprehensive training package on the implementation of the Birds and Habitats Directives (BHD) was developed and delivered. It strengthened the knowledge of NAPA and RAPA staff on EU nature legislation and clarified the relationship between the Natura 2000 network and Albania's traditional protected area categories. The materials were translated into Albanian and adapted to national and regional contexts, providing standardized introductory learning resources for RAPA staff and key local partners. These materials were subsequently used as core technical inputs for regional capacity building activities, ensuring consistent content, improved accessibility for practitioners, and a shared baseline of knowledge across institutions involved in protected area management.
A.1.3.2: As part of the projects support for field operations, seven drones were procured for RAPAs and Vjosa River national park Administration (ZAPK) in the projects pilot protected areas to strengthen surveillance, mapping, and biodiversity monitoring. Firefighting equipment was provided to six areas the seventh area, Vlora, had already been equipped under a previous project. Regarding sustainability, UNDP confirms that all equipment is formally included in NAPAs inventory. This ensures that NAPA allocates budget resources for maintenance and servicing, including equipment used at the RAPA level.
A.1.3.4: To strengthen NAPA and RAPA capacity to meet EU monitoring and reporting requirements, the project has focused on training in the use of METT4 as an integral part of the monitoring and reporting framework.
